additionalInformation: The following students are precluded from taking this course: Mathematics majors, Quantitative Finance majors, Data Science and Analytics majors, Data Science and Applied AI (DSAAI) majors, Data Science and Economics (DSE) majors, Statistics majors, Mathematics second majors, Quantitative Finance second majors, Data Analytics second majors, Statistics second majors, School of Computing students, Engineering students from the College of Design and Engineering (CDE)
description: Data is the language of information: to work with data is to study change, structure, and uncertainty. This course presents a gentle introduction to programming while developing the mathematical foundations of modern data analysis: calculus to quantify change, linear algebra to uncover structure, and probability to make sense of randomness. Topics include differentiation and integration with applications to optimisation; linear systems, vectors, and matrices, culminating in the Spectral Theorem; and probability, random variables, discrete and continuous distributions, and the Central Limit Theorem. Strong emphasis is placed on computation and simulation to build intuition, fluency, and confidence in working with data.
